name: Meshuallam
overview: Meshuallam was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Hodaviah. His mention in Scripture is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes or narrative details provided. This limited information situates him within the post-exilic community of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Meshuallam means 'restitution,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with no indication that it was given directly by God. This meaning may imply a theme of restoration or compensation, though the text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Meshuallam was the son of Hodaviah. It is also inferred that Sallu was his father, indicating a generational lineage within the Benjaminite family. Beyond these relationships, no other family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Meshuallam's significance lies in his inclusion within the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin, as detailed in 1 Chronicles 9:7. Such genealogies served to affirm the identity and continuity of the Israelite community after the exile. Though not a prominent figure in narrative accounts, his presence underscores the faithfulness of God's people through successive generations.
